differences: The Methods give 4.36% of trials removed in the looming-cue experiment; the shared file has 4.17% without a hand angle (the 12.01% of the internal-monitoring experiment reproduces).

The Results give mean participant median reaction times of 408.64 and 347.57 ms for the 500 and 1500 ms delays (t(21) = -8.15) in the internal-monitoring experiment; the median rtGoSig of the training trials gives 397.98 and 345.77 ms (t(21) = -8.49), so the authors' RT measure is not recovered. The looming-cue reaction times (275.00 and 286.02 ms) cannot be checked because that file has no reaction times.

The Methods call the training feedback 'a fixed cursor rotation of +15 or -15 deg', the Figure 1 legend a fixed ('clamped') cursor trajectory 15 deg off the reach direction that participants ignored; it is coded as an error clamp. The model-fitting text also describes the error as the rotation minus the hand angle.
The third experiment (discrete numeric cues, 9 participants after exclusions) and the participants excluded in the paper (2 and 4 in the first two experiments) are not in the deposit.
